citations.excerpt: We present YOLO, a new approach to object detection. Prior work on object detection repurposes classifiers to perform detection. Instead, we frame object detection as a regression problem to spatially separated bounding boxes and associated class probabilities. A single neural network predicts bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in one evaluation. Since the whole detection pipeline is a single network, it can be optimized end-to-end directly on detection performance. Our unified architecture is extremely fast. Our base YOLO model processes images in real-time at 45 frames per second. A smaller version of the network, Fast YOLO, processes an astounding 155 frames per second while still achieving double the mAP of other real-time detectors. Compared to state-of-the-art detection systems, YOLO makes more localization errors but is less likely to predict false positives on background. Finally, YOLO learns very general representations of objects. It outperforms other detection methods, including DPM and R-CNN, when generalizing from natural images to other domains like artwork.

baseline.answer:
### Сравнение подходов к детекции объектов в реальном времени: YOLO и RT-DETR

**Сходства:**

- Оба подхода направлены на достижение высокой скорости обработки изображений, что делает их пригодными для приложений в реальном времени, таких как автономное вождение и видеонаблюдение.
- Оба метода используют глубокие нейронные сети для обнаружения объектов и оптимизированы для повышения точности и производительности.

**Различия:**

- **YOLO (You Only Look Once)** формулирует задачу детекции как проблему регрессии, предсказывая ограничивающие рамки и вероятности классов напрямую из полного изображения за одну итерацию. Это позволяет достичь высокой скорости: базовая модель обрабатывает 45 кадров в секунду, а ускоренная версия — до 155 кадров в секунду [1].
- **RT-DETR (Real-Time DEtection TRansformer)**, в свою очередь, представляет собой энд-ту-энд детектор на основе трансформеров, который устраняет необходимость в постобработке NMS (Non-Maximum Suppression). Вместо этого RT-DETR использует эффективный гибридный энкодер для быстрой обработки многомасштабных признаков и улучшает качество начальных запросов к декодеру, что повышает точность. RT-DETR-R50 достигает 108 FPS на GPU T4, превосходя YOLO по скорости и точности [2].

Таким образом, YOLO делает упор на скорость за счет регрессионного подхода, в то время как RT-DETR предлагает альтернативу, устраняя NMS и используя архитектуру трансформеров для достижения сопоставимой или лучшей производительности.

cases.question: Summarize what is known in ws-pilot-od about one-stage detectors vs two-stage detectors, in 5–8 bullet points, and say what is uncertain.

baseline.answer:
- YOLO (You Only Look Once) is a one-stage object detector that frames detection as a single regression problem, predicting bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in one evaluation.
- It unifies the entire detection pipeline into a single neural network, enabling end-to-end optimization and real-time performance, with the base model processing images at 45 FPS and a smaller version (Fast YOLO) reaching 155 FPS.
- Compared to two-stage detectors like Fast R-CNN, YOLO avoids separate region proposal and classification stages, making it faster but more prone to localization errors.
- YOLO tends to produce fewer false positives on background compared to state-of-the-art two-stage detectors, trading off some localization accuracy for higher speed and overall efficiency.
- Traditional two-stage systems such as R-CNN variants rely on a disjoint pipeline: extracting features, running classifiers or localizers on sliding windows or region subsets, and refining bounding boxes—steps that are unified in YOLO.
- YOLO outperforms methods like DPM and R-CNN when generalizing from natural images to other domains such as artwork, indicating stronger generalization due to its end-to-end learned representations.
- In error analysis, YOLO makes more localization mistakes than Fast R-CNN but suffers less from false detections, highlighting a key trade-off between accuracy types.
- The system is compared directly to DPM and Fast R-CNN, showing superior speed and mAP among real-time detectors, though specific comparative metrics on newer two-stage models are not detailed.

**Uncertain aspects:**
- The exact year and venue of the YOLO paper are absent from metadata.
- There is no explicit mention of later one-stage detectors (e.g., SSD, RetinaNet) or comparisons with more recent two-stage architectures (e.g., Faster R-CNN with attention).

- One-stage detectors like YOLO are extremely fast, with the base model processing images at 45 frames per second and a smaller version (Fast YOLO) reaching 155 frames per second, making them suitable for real-time applications.
- In contrast, two-stage detectors such as R-CNN and its variants typically involve a region proposal step followed by classification, which makes them slower but often more accurate in certain aspects.
- YOLO outperforms other real-time detection methods in mean Average Precision (mAP), achieving more than double the mAP of prior real-time systems while maintaining high speed.
- While YOLO makes fewer false positive predictions on background, it tends to suffer more from localization errors compared to two-stage detectors like Fast R-CNN.
- The unified end-to-end trainable architecture of YOLO allows for direct optimization on detection performance, unlike traditional pipelines that repurpose classifiers.
- YOLO demonstrates strong generalization capabilities, outperforming methods like DPM and R-CNN when applied to domains beyond natural images, such as artwork.

## 3. Comparison to Other Detection Systems

Object detection is a core problem in computer vision. Detection pipelines generally start by extracting a set of robust features from input images (Haar [25], SIFT [23], HOG [4], convolutional features [6]). Then, classifiers [36, 21, 13, 10] or localizers [1, 32] are used to identify objects in the feature space. These classifiers or localizers are run either in sliding window fashion over the whole image or on some subset of regions in the image [35, 15, 39]. We compare the YOLO detection system to several top detection frameworks, highlighting key similarities and differences.

## Abstract

We present YOLO, a new approach to object detection. Prior work on object detection repurposes classifiers to perform detection. Instead, we frame object detection as a regression problem to spatially separated bounding boxes and associated class probabilities. A single neural network predicts bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in one evaluation. Since the whole detection pipeline is a single network, it can be optimized end-to-end directly on detection performance.

Our unified architecture is extremely fast. Our base YOLO model processes images in real-time at 45 frames per second. A smaller version of the network, Fast YOLO, processes an astounding 155 frames per second while still achieving double the mAP of other real-time detectors. Compared
